metadata.Name: PIQA
metadata.Description: Physical Interaction: Question Answering (PIQA) is a benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning. The task is multiple-choice question answering, where given a goal (e.g., 'To separate egg whites from the yolk...'), a model must choose the more sensible of two solutions. The dataset was created by human annotators inspired by the website instructables.com, focusing on everyday situations and atypical solutions.
Provider: Paul G. Allen School for Computer Science and Engineering, University of Washington
metadata.Paper Title: PIQA: Reasoning about Physical Commonsense in Natural Language
Affiliations: Paul G. Allen School for Computer Science and Engineering, University of Washington
metadata.Abstract: Questions requiring this kind of physical commonsense pose a challenge to today’s natural language understanding systems. While recent pretrained models (such as BERT) have made progress on question answering over more abstract domains – such as news articles and encyclopedia entries, where text is plentiful – in more physical domains, text is inherently limited due to reporting bias. Can AI systems learn to reliably answer physical commonsense questions without experiencing the physical world? In this paper, we introduce the task of physical commonsense reasoning and a corresponding benchmark dataset Physical Interaction: Question Answering or PIQA. Though humans find the dataset easy (95% accuracy), large pretrained models struggle (∼77%). We provide analysis about the dimensions of knowledge that existing models lack, which offers significant opportunities for future research.
